        "The full owned diff changes only antyhing to anything in the PerformExpand comment. The SyncFolderList call and no-op lambda are byte-for-byte unchanged by this patch; there is no executable fix or changed test.",
        "Historical SyncFolderList obtains the opaque folder state token, defines owning callbacks for root/folder metadata changes and token storage, moves postSyncCallback into EwsFolderSyncListener, then returns the client SyncFolderHierarchy call. EwsFolderSyncListener::OnSuccess forwards to the stored callback. PerformExpand supplies a callback that returns NS_OK and requests no follow-on message synchronization. GetNewMessages and PerformBiff use different callbacks that fetch messages after folder-list synchronization.",
        "The accepted comparison uses ExchangeIncomingServer.cpp at the fixed revision, separately from the legacy EwsIncomingServer.cpp owned diff. PerformExpand retains the corrected comment and no-op callback. Later accepted SyncFolderList resets status feedback on success and error, then invokes postSyncCallback even on error; the comment explains continuing Biff for existing folders. No-op NS_OK does not prove remote folder sync succeeded. The later Biff listener/state machinery is not attributed to this typo patch.",
        "Current direct test callers invoke performExpand and wait for the expected Inbox/custom folder before reading it. The notifications test asserts zero initial unread messages, later adds a remote message and calls performBiff before checking the alert. The item-operation test explicitly calls syncFolder after expansion before asserting zero destination messages. These are static test assertions, not executed results. The about3Pane expansion caller is guarded to IMAP, so it is not evidence that this UI handler calls EWS PerformExpand.",
        "The corrected local comment accurately explains why this caller supplies a no-op continuation. Existing aMsgWindow, postSyncCallback, EwsFolderSyncListener and accepted Exchange names retain their distinct roles; this source does not establish a general lambda/comment naming rule. No new assertions or test setup were written. No test, build, lint, server, or UI ran.",
